facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Ravana abducted Kausalya immediately prior to her wedding, and placed her in a box on a deserted island in the middle of the ocean.
facts.text: The narrative of Ravana abducting Rama's mother Kaushalya prior to her wedding is found in the Sara Kanda of the medieval Sanskrit text Ananda Ramayana.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Brahma responded that the son of Kausalya and Dasharatha would be the cause of his death.
facts.text: According to the Ananda Ramayana, Ravana imprisoned Kaushalya in a box on a secluded sea island after Brahma revealed that her future son would bring about his demise.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Dasharatha chanced upon the box in which she was enclosed and they were married inside the box.
facts.text: In the Ananda Ramayana story, King Dasharatha survives a sea ambush by Ravana, discovers Kaushalya inside the wooden chest on the island, and completes a Gandharva marriage with her inside the enclosure.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: However most modern scholars agree that it is a later medieval text composed during the 15th century AD, and not an original composition by Valmiki.
facts.text: Textual historians date the composition of the Ananda Ramayana to around the fifteenth century CE, whereas traditional religious attribution credits the work to sage Valmiki.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Its primary significance, however, is its inclusion of original stories that are intended to provide background information for the Valmiki Ramayana narrative.
facts.text: Folklorists identify the motif of a demonic king abducting a royal bride after hearing a birth prophecy as a narrative borrowing influenced by the Bhagavata Purana's account of Kamsa, Devaki, and Krishna.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: This excavation confirmed that Ayodhya was first occupied in the 7th century BCE.
facts.source_name: ASI, Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites Project
facts.text: Archaeological excavations at Ayodhya during the 1975 to 1976 season of the 'Archaeology of Ramayana Sites' project documented the earliest continuous human settlement levels dating to the 7th century BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The ASI submitted a 574-page report before the court that suggested a chronology through different periods starting from the Northern Black Polished Ware culture.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India's 2003 excavation report on Ayodhya identified Northern Black Polished Ware cultural layers at the lowest stratified horizons of the site.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: It confirmed that Ram Setu is a continuous 29-km submarine ridge rising 8 metres above the seabed from Dhanushkodi to Talaimannar.
facts.text: Satellite bathymetry conducted by the Indian Space Research Organisation mapped Adam's Bridge as a continuous 29-kilometre submerged chain of limestone shoals between Dhanushkodi and Mannar Island.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Geological Survey of India views the underlying ridge as a natural marine landform shaped by currents and sediment deposition, while alternative views argue for man-made layering.
facts.source_name: Geological Survey of India / Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
facts.text: The Geological Survey of India classifies Adam's Bridge as a natural barrier formation shaped by marine currents, while proponents of underwater archaeology argue core samples may indicate deliberate ancient modification.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Excavations at Sravasti revealed fortifications and habitation layers associated with ancient Kosala from the mid-first millennium BCE.
facts.text: Excavations conducted by the Archaeological Survey of India at the ancient Kosala capital of Sravasti revealed fortifications and urban occupation layers dating from the 6th century BCE.

intro.prompt: 16:9 landscape, 1920x1080, about 8 seconds, high-energy and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: a riverbank at sunrise, the water and far bank at Ravan behind, colourful and lively, a shallow depth of field. Lighting: bright high-key light, warm and punchy, crisp on the face, a gentle rim light on the hair; no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] walking and talking, then stopping suddenly and turning to face the camera on the key word, one open palm raised, wearing a maroon sweater over a white collar. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, friendly eye contact with the lens. Delivery: bubbling over with excitement like a TV news reporter who has just found an amazing story and cannot wait to share it: a warm, genuine smile and bright wide eyes, delighted and amazed, never angry; pitch jumps on the key word, a half-second pause before the number, a big grin on the reveal, open inviting gestures; no scowl, no frown, no glaring, no shouting at the viewer; never flat, never calm, never monotone. Body language in three beats: on the question, an incredulous head shake and open palms; on the second line, a small beat of the open hand on each key word; on "Ab suniye, ye chaunkane wali baat hai!", a wink-like nod and a hand beckoning the viewer in. Prop: a printed photograph or old map of the place, held up to the camera for a moment, held low at first and lifted toward the lens on the second line, then lowered. Camera: handheld tracking shot that walks backward with him, slight natural shake, medium shot to medium close-up. @SGMythWorld watermark top right, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue screen anywhere in the frame; the only object in his hands or near him is the prop.
